problem: Audit persistence has multiple owners and hidden context dependencies through global GORM callbacks.
acceptance_criteria: No production code uses audit constructors, setters, update-map helpers, or actor hydration hooks.
Every audited create explicitly assigns created and updated actor type and ID columns.
Every audited update explicitly assigns updated actor type and ID columns.
No GORM audit callback remains registered.
Existing database and public API contracts remain compatible.
Missing or invalid actors fail before database execution.
Required tests and repository finalization pass.
risks: A missed write site may persist null audit columns.
A missed update site may retain stale updated-actor values.
Removing hydration may break response conversion if a mapper still reads transient actor fields.
The migration cannot safely deploy partially after callback removal.
implementation_steps: Inventory all creates and updates for models embedding Mutable.
Resolve actors from explicit authentication arguments at service boundaries.
Populate all create audit columns directly in model literals.
Populate update audit columns directly in update maps or models.
Convert response actors directly from persisted columns.
Remove callbacks, registration, hydration, and mutation helpers.
Run focused package tests and repository finalization.
rollback: Revert the implementation commit as one unit. No database rollback is required.
